newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament demands more aid for orphans.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament demands more aid for orphans.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday urged the European Union to find more money to help orphans, psychiatric patients and the aged living in dire conditions in the former Soviet bloc.

Euro-MPs said in a resolution that absolute poverty had soared in the 18 Central and Eastern Europe countries (CEEC) since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1989 while government spending on care institutions and social security had plummeted.

The EU assembly urged the 15-member EU bloc to work with the CEEC governments to improve conditions for the more than one million children living in care in these countries, which are candidates for EU membership.
The resolution called for more EU aid -- through both governments and non-governmental relief agencies -- for CEEC psychiatric hospitals, old people's homes, schools and social security systems.

Parliament's appeal responds to a report published last month by the United Nations Children's Fund, UNICEF, which said children in these countries now faced worse deprivation than during the communist era.
UNICEF said social impoverishment meant too many children were being abandoned to state care, while the leap in adult mortality rates had pushed up the number of orphans.

The report recalled the inhumane conditions in Romania's orphanages, revealed after the fall of President Nicolae Ceaucescu seven years ago, and warned that appalling conditions continued both in Romania and in other post-communist countries.
